result.question:
The last maintenance job on Transformer 1 at site MAIN was supposed to deal with the gassing, and I want to know whether it actually worked.

Find the most recently closed work order on Transformer 1. Give me its number, description, completion date, resolution notes and failure code, and tell me which fault it was meant to fix.

Then look at the oil samples taken after that date, within 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. Use hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co. Screen hydrogen, acetylene and co for anomalous samples with a proper anomaly detection model rather than a fixed threshold. Separately, run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample and compare its fault class with the fault the job was meant to fix.

Decide as follows:
- If both checks point to trouble, meaning at least one anomaly is flagged and the classification still shows the same fault or a higher-energy one, call the fix ineffective. Create a priority 2 corrective follow-up work order that references the original work order number, and code it with the closest failure code from our catalog.
- If only one of the two checks points to trouble, don't create a corrective job. Recommend a confirmatory oil resample within 7 days and say which check disagreed.
- If neither points to trouble, say the fix appears to have held.

If the closed job was oil filtration, degassing or regeneration, the gas levels will have been reset. In that case, judge the result on the rate of change after the job, not on absolute levels, and say you did so.

If no work order on Transformer 1 was closed before or during the window, say so, use all samples in the window, and give only the classification and anomaly result without a verdict on any fix. If fewer than 4 samples fall after the completion date, skip the anomaly model and compare the first and last post-job values instead.
result.answer:
## Result

**No closed work order exists on Transformer 1 at MAIN.**

I checked the work order system: there are 6 work orders on Transformer 1 (OUTAGE-T1-COND4, DGA-T1-MONTHLY, 1000051, 1000052, 1000046, 1000045 — the last two are on other assets), but **none has status COMP or CLOSE**. The most relevant ones (1000051 OLTC inspection, 1000052 oil retest, OUTAGE-T1-COND4) are still WAPPR/APPR — i.e., not yet closed. Per your instruction, since no WO was closed before or during the window, I used all samples in the window and give only the classification and anomaly result, with no verdict on any fix.

### Samples in window (2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19)

| Date | H2 | CH4 | C2H6 | C2H4 | C2H2 | CO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15 | 2845 | 7406 | 5467 | 16684 | 7 | 32 |
| 2024-01-16 | 2950 | 7200 | 5400 | 16500 | 6 | 30 |
| 2024-01-17 | 2800 | 7300 | 5500 | 16700 | 8 | 35 |
| 2024-01-18 | 2900 | 7350 | 5450 | 16600 | 7 | 33 |

### Anomaly screening (hydrogen, acetylene, CO)

I could not run a proper anomaly-detection model: the model catalog contains only one active model (`ttm_96_28`, a forecasting-only TinyTimeMixer), with **no anomaly-detection model available**, and the `interpret_dga` / DGA fault-classification tool returned "LLM unavailable" on repeated attempts, so no Rogers Ratio classification result could be produced either.

As a fallback descriptive read of the four samples (not a model-based verdict): hydrogen (2800–2950 ppm), acetylene (6–8 ppm) and CO (30–35 ppm) are all **flat/noisy with no trend** — no sample stands out as a clear step-change in these three gases. Ethylene is the dominant gas (~16.5–16.7k ppm), consistent with a high-temperature thermal fault in oil, which matches the T3 (700–1000 °C) classification referenced in WO 1000052's notes.

### Summary
- **Work order number / description / completion date / resolution notes / failure code:** not applicable — no closed WO on Transformer 1 exists.
- **Fault the job was meant to fix:** per WO 1000052 notes, a **T3 thermal fault in oil (700–1000 °C)**, likely OLTC-related (WO 1000051).
- **Anomaly model result:** unavailable (no anomaly-detection model in catalog); descriptive view shows no anomalous samples among hydrogen/acetylene/CO.
- **DGA classification (latest complete sample, 2024-01-18):** the IEC 60599 Rogers Ratio tool failed ("LLM unavailable") on multiple retries, so I cannot report a confirmed fault class. The gas profile is consistent with a thermal fault in oil (T2/T3), matching the fault the open WOs target.
- **No verdict on fix effectiveness** is given, per your rule for no closed work order.

Recommendation: once OUTAGE-T1-COND4 / 1000051 / 1000052 are completed, re-run this assessment with a closed-WO completion date, and re-try the DGA classification once the interpretation service is available.
